questions.text: In a proscenium theater, what is the generally accepted minimum dimension for the stage opening and the ratio of backstage area to stage area?

options.text: 9.0 m × 12.0 m; Backstage = 30-50% of stage area
6.0 m × 9.0 m; Backstage = 10% of stage area
12.0 m × 15.0 m; Backstage = 100% of stage area
No standard; varies by theater seat count

rationale.b: Too small for standard theatrical scenery.
rationale.d: Functional requirements for performance (scenery, lighting) dictate size more than seat count.
rationale.correct: While not mandated by PD 1096, architectural standards for a functional proscenium stage typically start at 9m x 12m with a support area of 30-50% to accommodate wings and scenery.
rationale.takeaway: Theatrical dimensions are governed by performance standards, not building code minimums.

questions.text: What is the minimum width for a level exit aisle in an assembly venue like a theater according to the RA 9514 2019 Revised IRR?

rationale.a: This is below the minimum clear width for public assembly aisles.
rationale.b: Correct; 915 mm is the standard minimum for aisles.
rationale.c: Often cited as a corridor minimum, but aisles have a specific 915 mm threshold.
rationale.d: A recommended width for high-traffic, but not the statutory minimum.
rationale.correct: RA 9514 2019 IRR Section 10.2.13.1.6 specifies that the minimum clear width of any aisle shall not be less than 915 mm (36 inches).

questions.text: A 250-seat theater has a backstage area of 50 sqm used for storage and technical support. Calculate the total building occupant load for egress design.

rationale.a: Ignores staff/technical occupancy in support areas.
rationale.b: Correct; combines fixed seating with staff storage density ($27.9$).
rationale.c: Uses the Dense Stage factor ($1.4$) for the entire backstage area.
rationale.correct: 1. Seating: 250 occupants (fixed count). 2. Backstage (Storage/Mechanical): $50 \text{ sqm} \div 27.9 = 1.79 \approx 2$ occupants. Total = $250 + 2 = 252$.
rationale.takeaway: Sum all functional areas. Storage/Technical support uses $27.9$ sqm/person.

questions.text: A 1,500-seat multipurpose venue uses flexible temporary staging instead of a fixed proscenium. Under PD 1096, what is its classification?

options.text: Group H Division 2 (Assembly without stage, ≥ 300 occupants)
Group I (Assembly with stage, ≥ 1,000 occupants) because the venue exceeds the 1,000 seat threshold
Group H Division 1 (Assembly with stage, < 1,000 occupants) because staging is present even if temporary
Group J (Open-air assembly) because the flexible staging creates a non-permanent performance configuration

rationale.a: Correct; lack of a permanent stage triggers the 'without stage' classification.
rationale.correct: PD 1096 Section 701 classifies assembly buildings without a stage and with an occupant load of 300 or more as Group H Division 2.
rationale.takeaway: Classification depends on structural presence (Fixed Stage) rather than intent (Multipurpose Use).

questions.text: A 350-seat theater provides one 1.5 m door and one 1.2 m stair. Based on RA 9514 2019 IRR, is this adequate egress for an assembly occupancy?

options.text: Yes, aggregate width and count are met, assuming no additional exits are required by local amendments.
No, assembly occupancies require a minimum of 2 separate exits regardless of width.
No, the width is insufficient for 350 persons, especially during peak occupancy events.
Yes, if the travel distance is less than 45 meters, and no other obstructions are present.

rationale.b: Correct; the 'remoteness' and 'separation' of the 2 exits is the critical factor for assembly safety.
rationale.c: Required width is $350 \times 7.6 = 2,660$ mm. Available is $2,700$ mm. Width is technically sufficient, but count/remoteness is the priority.
rationale.correct: RA 9514 Section 10.2.13.1.1 mandates that every assembly occupancy shall be provided with at least two separate means of egress. One door and one stair satisfy the count of 2, but they must be 'separate' and remote from each other.
rationale.takeaway: Assembly rule: Minimum 2 exits, remotely located, aggregate width satisfied.

questions.text: What is the typical recommended row spacing (front-to-front) in general architectural practice for theater seating to ensure adequate legroom?

rationale.a: Too narrow; physically impossible for standard theater chairs.
rationale.b: Correct; aligns with international and local design standards.
rationale.c: Excessive; reduces capacity without significant added benefit for standard theaters.
rationale.correct: While PD 1096 and RA 9514 focus on clear widths between rows for egress, general architectural practice (UAP/Neufert) recommends 850–1,050 mm front-to-front spacing for comfort.
rationale.takeaway: Row spacing is a design guideline (850-1,050 mm), not a building code minimum.

questions.text: What is the minimum net seating area floor space (in sqm) required for a 200-seat theater per RA 9514 2019 IRR?

rationale.c: Assumes $1.0$ sqm per person, which is not a code standard for fixed seating.
rationale.d: Uses $0.60$, which is too dense for fixed seating.
rationale.correct: RA 9514 2019 IRR Table 10.2.7.3.1 specifies an occupant load factor of $0.84$ sqm per person (net) for assembly areas with fixed seats. $200 \times 0.84 = 168$ sqm.
rationale.takeaway: Theater Fixed Seating Factor = $0.84$ sqm/person (Net Area).

questions.text: A theater with 500 occupants has two 1.2 m doors and one 1.5 m stairwell. Is the aggregate exit width compliant under RA 9514 (2019 IRR)?

rationale.a: Correct; correctly calculates both required and provided aggregate widths.
rationale.b: Fails to include the stairwell width in the aggregate total.
rationale.d: Incorrectly uses a different factor or higher occupancy count.
rationale.correct: Required width for stairs = $500 \times 7.6 = 3,800$ mm. Available width = $1.2 + 1.2 + 1.5 = 3.9$ m ($3,900$ mm). Since $3,900 \ge 3,800$, it is compliant.
rationale.takeaway: Aggregate width must satisfy the most restrictive component (Stairs = $7.6$ mm/person).

questions.text: A theater has 300 fixed seats arranged in rows and a traditional proscenium stage (9.0 m × 12.0 m). Under PD 1096, what occupancy group classification applies?

options.text: Group H Division 1 (Assembly with stage, occupant load < 1,000)
Group I (Assembly with stage, occupant load ≥ 1,000), typically used for larger venues such as concert halls
Group C (Education and Recreation), which includes facilities like schools and community centers
Group H Division 2 (Assembly without stage), applicable to open-air venues or those without a defined stage area

rationale.a: Correct; the presence of a stage and capacity < 1,000 defines H-1.
rationale.b: Group I is reserved for assembly buildings with a stage and 1,000 or more occupants.
rationale.c: Group C is strictly for Educational institutions (Schools).
rationale.d: Division 2 applies to assembly buildings without a stage.
rationale.correct: PD 1096 Rule VII Table VII.1 classifies assembly buildings with a stage and an occupant load of less than 1,000 as Group H Division 1.
rationale.takeaway: The classification of theaters depends on two triggers: 1) Presence of a stage, and 2) Occupant load (threshold at 1,000).

questions.text: What is the minimum number of parking slots required for a theater with 600 seats according to the NBCP?

rationale.correct: PD 1096 Table VII.1 specifies 1 parking slot per 50 seats for theaters, cinemas, and auditoria. Calculation: $600 \div 50 = 12$ slots.
